title: Runtime validation: typeof guards and schema libraries
hook: TypeScript disappears at runtime. Every fetch, webhook, and env var is an untyped blob until you prove its shape — typeof guards for primitives, schema libraries for nested objects.

blocks.text: **Runtime shape validation** checks that a value actually matches what your code assumes before you use it. **typeof** and **Array.isArray** cover primitives and arrays; **in** and optional chaining help with presence; **schema libraries** (Zod, Valibot, AJV) parse nested objects with coercion rules and error paths. This is the JavaScript answer to C# model binding + DataAnnotations — except you choose where validation runs (handler edge, not compiler).

entries.plainDefinition: Function or check that narrows a value's type for TypeScript and protects runtime logic.
Declarative description of allowed shape, used to parse or reject input.
entries.example: const User = z.object({ id: z.string(), role: z.enum(['admin', 'member']) });

entries.plainDefinition: parse throws on failure; safeParse returns { success, data | error } for HTTP handlers.
Line where untrusted data enters — HTTP, WebSocket, localStorage, process.env.
entries.example: Validate once at controller; trust shape inside domain layer.

blocks.text: A missing field on a webhook payload becomes `undefined.role.toLowerCase()` and a 500 instead of a 400. Config typos in production only surface when code reads `port.toString()`. Senior teams validate **once at the edge**, map to domain types, and never re-parse deep in the stack. C# catches many issues at compile time; JS/TS teams duplicate intent: types for developers, schemas for runtime.

blocks.title: Interview trap: typeof null
blocks.body: typeof null === 'object' is a famous JS bug. Senior guard: value !== null && typeof value === 'object'. Schema libraries handle this consistently.

snippet.label: Manual typeof guards
snippet.explanation: Explicit guards for flat shapes. Throws TypeError — in HTTP layer map to 400 with field names.

snippet.label: Zod schema at API edge
snippet.explanation: safeParse returns discriminated result — no try/catch for expected validation failures.

snippet.label: C# model validation contrast
snippet.explanation: ASP.NET binds JSON to DTO at runtime with validation attributes — analogous to Zod.parse at the JS handler.

snippet.label: Failure mode: trusting JSON.parse
snippet.explanation: JSDoc or as-casts do not validate. Enum-like fields need runtime checks or schema.parse.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Validating in every helper instead of once at boundary. Using truthy checks for numbers (0 is valid). Casting with 'as User' after JSON.parse. Returning 500 for client shape errors instead of 400 with field paths.

blocks.text: Production: colocate schemas with OpenAPI or tRPC routers; version schemas when APIs evolve. Performance: AJV compiles JSON Schema once — good for high-throughput gateways; Zod ergonomics trade some speed. Security: validation is not sanitization — still escape output, still rate-limit. Pair with branded types in TS so validated output gets a distinct type via z.infer.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'we use TypeScript so we do not need runtime checks' for external input. Not knowing typeof null === 'object'. Cannot describe safeParse versus parse or where to validate in a layered architecture.

interviewTakeaways: Runtime validation proves shape after JSON.parse — TypeScript does not exist at runtime.
Validate once at trust boundaries; map to domain types inside.
typeof null is 'object' — use explicit null checks or schemas.
60s: External data needs schemas or guards. Zod safeParse for HTTP 400s. C# has model binding; JS you wire it. TS z.infer links compile and runtime.
Follow-up: how would you migrate a schema when a field becomes required?
commonPitfalls: Casting parsed JSON with 'as' instead of parsing through a schema.
Scattering validation logic across dozens of functions.
Strong answer: boundary validation, structured 400 errors, z.infer or equivalent, never trust fetch without parse.

jsTsCorrelations.note: function isUser(x): x is User pairs manual guards with TS narrowing; Zod infers TS types from the same schema used at runtime.
Every JSON.parse returns any shape — same problem as C# deserializing to object without a typed DTO.
